items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] So could King Oliver play then? King Oliver? ... [INTERVIEWER] No, no. King Oliver was a man listening, playing music, long listening.

ctx.x: Look at the fuel cost here now. Four and five, $6,000. You got a bear person in, save what? $50 in. Big fuel, isn't it? Look at the cost here now. That's true. You got to go in the thousand now. This is the bear person now. Oh, yeah.
So could King Oliver play then? King Oliver?

Yeah. Oh, man. What's he? If his name was King, what's nobody about that man, man? Who got food that man? If he was King, what's nobody about that man, man? No, no. If you're king and you prove that you're king, I'm going to jump on you? No, no. Let you know. That's what I'm going to have. Oh, yeah. Well, I thought maybe you were older than him.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Ori used to play a tram on... Uh, uh, uh, with King Oliver.

ctx.x: Really? What was Howard playing? Yes. Trumpet.

Trumpet and trombone and that's all? That's all. We played, we played in 55, Broadway, when Joyce took sick. We didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no trumpet. We did not have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no, we didn't have no clinic. And Joyce took sick. And Lewis Alcombe come, that, that night even his wife was our guest. Mm-hmm. And Joyce played two numbers, they, two, three numbers, they took sick. And me and Howard played the whole dance with…

Oh yeah, we had a piano. He was playing that night. Yeah, he played piano. But I mean you played parties with just trumpet and trumpet on no rhythm? No, no rhythm. No rhythm. Well, how did you keep the beat going? Beat with your feet.
